extracted.intended_audience: CIPO patent examiners and patent applicants/agents (Canada)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on drafting Final Actions, handling applicant responses, conducting Commissioner/PAB review, and patent maintenance/expiry procedures under the Canadian Patent Act and Patent Rules. Covers examiner practices, review panels, hearings, Commissioner decisions, and maintenance-fee obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid identifying defects for the first time in a Final Action
rubrics_metrics.description: While occasionally necessary, identifying a defect for the first time in a Final Action is generally not desirable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a major defect (anticipation, obviousness, lack of utility, non-statutory subject-matter, insufficiency, etc.) was overlooked in prior prosecution, a further regular requisition identifying the defect is most likely necessary so the applicant has opportunity to respond prior to rejection. If a new, significant defect was introduced by applicant amendments made in response to the previous report, the examiner must exercise judgement whether a Final Action is appropriate. However, where a new defect is readily understandable and easily fixed (e.g. missing antecedent, incorrect claim numbering), it may not be necessary to delay rejection. Do not ignore an identified defect to simplify the Final Action; decide whether the defect requires a further report under subsection 86(2) of the Patent Rules or can be included in a Final Action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Action report: opening and statement of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The opening paragraph of a Final Action will identify that it contains a requisition under subsection 86(5) of the Patent Rules, and will feature the words FINAL ACTION prominently; the report will also include an indication that the application is being rejected pursuant to subsection 86(3) (or subsection 199(1) where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the status and statutory basis clear at the outset so readers understand the nature of the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Action preamble: identify defects and claim status
rubrics_metrics.description: The preamble of the report should identify, in broad terms, the defects that have led to the rejection and which claims are considered defective and which are allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State which claims are central to the impasse and clearly identify any aspects of the claims that are central to the dispute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Action drafting objective: clarity on point of dispute
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal of the Final Action is to make the point of disagreement clear, to set out the applicant’s position as understood by the examiner, and the examiner’s reasoning for considering the application to still not comply with the Act or Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft so that interested persons (applicant, PAB, Commissioner, Court) can readily understand the dispute and examiner’s reasons despite applicant arguments. Note agreed facts or conclusions (with references) but do not comprehensively revisit them. Write the Final Action so it can be understood independently of other reports or responses (summarise rather than incorporate by reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Action content: recommended sections and information
rubrics_metrics.description: Although layout can be tailored, the following information should be provided where relevant: a summary of the application emphasizing relevant claims; identification of any allowable claims; identification of relevant prior art and discussion of pertinent teachings; summary of relevant prior prosecution; discussion of legal/jurisprudential/administrative considerations central to the dispute; grounds for rejection with comprehensive analysis including rebuttal of applicant arguments; and a brief summation recapitulating the grounds for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It may be beneficial to divide the report into sections with clear headings. Provide sufficient background (including applicant arguments) so the Final Action can be followed without referring to other documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to a Final Action: permissible applicant responses
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may respond to a Final Action by submitting amendments to make the application compliant with the Patent Act and Patent Rules or by submitting arguments as to why the application does comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon receipt of a response before expiry of time to respond, the examiner will review the application and consider whether the response overcomes the rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responses that overcome the rejection: allowance procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after considering amendments and arguments, the examiner considers that the application complies with the Act and Rules, it will be allowed pursuant to subsection 86(6) of the Patent Rules and the Commissioner must notify the applicant that the rejection is withdrawn, the application is allowable and require payment of the final fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Final Actions under former subsection 30(4), similar notice and final fee procedure applies per subsection 199(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Responses that do not overcome the rejection: examiner actions
rubrics_metrics.description: If after considering amendments and arguments the examiner considers the application still does not comply with the Act or Rules, next steps depend on whether the time to respond to the requisition has expired or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If time has not expired, examiner may contact applicant to inform conclusions and determine whether applicant wishes to submit further amendments/arguments prior to expiry (particularly where partial addressing occurred). If time has expired, subsection 86(7) applies: notify applicant rejection not withdrawn, any amendments made during the period beginning on the date of the final action and ending on the response deadline are deemed not to have been made, and the application must be reviewed by the Commissioner. Note that amendments after Final Action are deemed not made unless examiner determines they place the application in condition for allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of Reasons: purpose and content
rubrics_metrics.description: A Summary of Reasons is written by an examiner in preparation for the Commissioner’s review when the time to respond has expired and the applicant’s response has not overcome the rejection. It briefly sets out why the examiner still does not have reasonable grounds to believe the application complies with the Act and Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep it brief—do not comprehensively repeat the Final Action. Identify and address any new considerations arising from post-rejection correspondence (new arguments, jurisprudence, Office practice changes). Provide concise analysis of proposed amendments and note whether any proposed amendments would have overcome or partially addressed grounds for rejection or rendered claims allowable; identify defects in proposed amendments. Indicate if certain applicant arguments were compelling but insufficient (e.g., reliant on features not defined in claims). The Summary assists the PAB review by providing a concise, high-level overview of important considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of a rejected application: scope and intent
rubrics_metrics.description: A review of a rejected application (required by subsection 86(7)) is primarily focused on resolving the impasse but is also comprehensive—any apparent defects in the application, even beyond those indicated in the Final Action or Summary of Reasons, will be identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The intention is to achieve efficiency, finality, and compliance with the Patent Act and Rules while adhering to natural justice and procedural fairness. The review may be terminated by withdrawal, abandonment, or if the application remains abandoned outside reinstatement period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to the Patent Appeal Board (PAB)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner is assisted by the Patent Appeal Board in performing the review. The PAB is an advisory body of senior officials with prior examiner experience; review is typically by a panel of three members who must not have participated in prosecution of the application or given prior advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review occurs only after response time expired and Summary of Reasons forwarded. The review is ex parte (only the patent applicant is a party) and is performed at arm’s length from examination divisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications with applicant during review
rubrics_metrics.description: During review, the applicant can expect contact from the Board on administrative and substantive matters. The initial letter notifies the applicant the application has been transferred to the PAB, that the examiner’s rejection has not been withdrawn, and provides a copy of the Summary of Reasons. If applicant submitted amendments in response to Final Action, the initial letter confirms such amendments are considered not to have been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications from the PAB generally include a time period to respond but are not requisitions—failure to respond will not suspend the review nor cause abandonment. Additional information and offers of opportunity to be heard may be included or sent separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and handling of new defects during review
rubrics_metrics.description: If the panel identifies defects beyond those in the Final Action (due to different claim interpretation, jurisprudence, late-filed foreign art, or changes in Act/Rules), the applicant is given notice of the issue and an opportunity to respond, including proposing amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsection 86(9) requires notice and an invitation to submit arguments within one month. The panel may raise the matter directly with applicant or request an examiner analysis presented as a Supplemental Analysis (similar to a Summary of Reasons but addressing only the identified issue). If a Supplemental Analysis is requested, the applicant receives a copy and any response should only address the defect under consideration. In exceptional cases, panel may request further search and prior art analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification procedure during review
rubrics_metrics.description: The panel may seek clarifications to ensure common understanding of matters at issue (examiner’s grounds, applicant’s arguments, Office practice, or facts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A memo will set out matters requiring clarification; examiner input may be provided via a Supplemental Analysis. Applicant is given time to respond and may respond in writing or with oral arguments at the hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to be heard (hearing rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsection 86(13) specifies the applicant must be given an opportunity to be heard before any refusal; the applicant will generally be invited to participate in a hearing but is not required to attend (may elect written record).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel performs initial review before hearing to ensure issues are clearly identified. Hearing purpose: allow applicant to develop/explain reasons contending application is not defective or that proposed amendments overcome defects. Present written arguments/evidence well ahead of hearing; new legal/technical arguments or fresh evidence should be presented as early as possible (not deferred to review). Hearing may be in person, by teleconference or videoconference; participants may include panel, applicant and agent, examiner and supervisor. Hearing typically begins with applicant oral presentation; panel may question applicant; examiner and supervisor may be called to answer questions. No cross-questioning between applicant and examiner. Points of fact agreed or concessions will be taken into account. Panel makes recommendation to Commissioner; no final decision made at hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions without a hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: A hearing is not necessary in every case. The applicant may decline the invitation and the panel will provide a recommendation based on the written record. Also, if panel concludes application complies with Act and Rules, no hearing is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsection 86(13) does not require a hearing where application will be allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to the Commissioner: content and form
rubrics_metrics.description: At conclusion of panel review, the panel will deliberate and formulate a recommendation to the Commissioner in written reasons that generally include explanation of the invention, background prosecution information, identification of issues, relevant statutory authority, pertinent jurisprudence, summary of positions of examiner and applicant, detailed analysis including factual findings, and a final recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner is briefed on the case and reviews the recommendation prior to rendering a final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner’s Decision: reasoning and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner’s Decision provides reasons for arriving at the decision with reference to the Patent Act, Patent Rules and pertinent jurisprudence; typically adopts the panel’s reasons. A copy of the decision is sent to the applicant (registered mail if refused) and decisions become part of the public prosecution file (subject to limited exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner’s Decisions provide insight/guidance to applicants and examiners and are reviewed when practice guidance is provided. A database of published Commissioner’s Decisions is maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome — rejection withdrawn and application allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: If after review the Commissioner has reasonable grounds to believe the application complies with the Act and Rules, the Commissioner must inform the applicant that the rejection is withdrawn, the application has been found allowable and require payment of the final fee (subsection 86(10)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once allowed, application is treated as any other allowed application with notice of allowance and final fee requisition. Similar provisions apply for cases under former subsection 30(4) per subsection 199(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome — application refused and appeal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commissioner is of the view the examiner’s rejection is justified or the application does not comply and it is not evident it can be made compliant by directed amendment, the Commissioner will refuse the application pursuant to section 40 of the Patent Act and specify the six-month period to initiate an appeal to the Federal Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Federal Court has exclusive jurisdiction to hear the appeal; decisions may be appealed further to the Federal Court of Appeal and, with leave, to the Supreme Court of Canada.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner-required amendments under review
rubrics_metrics.description: If after review the Commissioner has reasonable grounds to believe certain amendments are necessary to make the application allowable, the Commissioner must inform the applicant that those amendments must be made within three months after the notice (subsection 86(11)) and invite the applicant to make the amendments under paragraph 101(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required amendments may be based on proposed amendments submitted during review or based on Commissioner’s findings. If applicant does not make necessary amendments, or makes amendments beyond those required, the Commissioner will refuse the application under section 40.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fees: when payment is required
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee must pay annual maintenance fees starting at the 2nd anniversary of the filing date to maintain the patent in effect (subsection 46(1) of the Patent Act and subsection 112(1) of the Patent Rules). If an additional term is granted, maintenance fees start on the 20th anniversary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amounts and time limits are posted on CIPO’s Patent Fees webpage. Maintenance fees are due on or before the anniversary of the filing date; fees may be paid in advance. Time limits for payment of maintenance fees for patents cannot be extended (subsection 112(4) and subsection 117.05(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — patent granted with outstanding application maintenance fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent is granted based on an application for which a maintenance fee that fell within the 12-month period was not paid before the patent issued, the unpaid maintenance fee amount will be added to the first maintenance fee after the patent is granted and a late fee will also be required (subsection 112(5) and subsection 117.05(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This adjusts payment obligations following grant when a prior application fee was unpaid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late and non-payment procedure and late fee period
rubrics_metrics.description: If the full required maintenance fee is not paid on or before the anniversary date, a late fee will also need to be paid. A Commissioner’s Notice will be sent shortly after the maintenance fee due date requiring payment of the maintenance fee and the late fee before the later of six months after the maintenance fee due date or two months after the date of the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The period between the original due date and the later of six months from the due date or two months from the notice date is the late fee period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deemed expiry of patents for unpaid maintenance fees
rubrics_metrics.description: If the maintenance fee and the late fee are not paid within the late fee period, the term of the patent will be deemed to have expired retroactively at the original maintenance fee due date (subsection 46(4) and section 113). The same applies to additional term expiration (subsection 46.2(4) and section 117.06).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deemed expiry is retroactive to the original due date and applies equally to additional-term patents where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courtesy letters for deemed expiry
rubrics_metrics.description: While not required by the Act or Rules, the Patent Office will endeavour to inform patentees of deemed expiry through a courtesy letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentees will have received a notice of potential deemed expiry if they did not comply with requirements to pay maintenance and late fees; courtesy letters are additional but not mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reversal of deemed expiry: grounds and statutory basis
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent (or additional term) is deemed to have expired under the Act/Rules, it is possible to request the Commissioner to reverse the deemed expiry under subsection 46(5) (or 46.2(5)) and related Patent Rules sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The deemed expiry will be reversed only if the Commissioner determines the failure occurred despite the due care required by the circumstances (paragraph 46(5)(b) or 46.2(5)(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time period for requesting reversal of deemed expiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Patent Rules, the time limit to request reversal of deemed expiry is 12 months after the end of six months after the applicable maintenance fee due date (with extensions under section 78 where the period expires on a prescribed or designated day).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An illustrative example is provided showing calculation of the late-fee period and the 12-month window for requesting reversal—practical attention to dates is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due care standard for reversal of deemed expiry (PLT implementation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to implement the Patent Law Treaty introduce a due care standard that must be met by a patentee to apply for reversal of deemed expiry of a patent or additional term because of a failure to pay maintenance fee and late fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commissioner must determine that the failure occurred in spite of the due care required by the circumstances before reversing the deemed expiry (paragraph 46(5)(b)/46.2(5)(b)). Transitional provisions apply to pre-October 30, 2019 due dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner’s determination of due care: patentee evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain a determination, the patentee must provide reasons for the failure to take required action to avoid deemed expiry. If the Commissioner determines the failure occurred despite due care, the deemed expiry is deemed never to have occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentee should submit a clear explanation and supporting evidence demonstrating that due care required by the circumstances was taken; the Commissioner assesses and decides whether to reverse deemed expiry.
